articles.title: Plano de Gestão da Orla de Natal: veja como participar da consulta | G1
articles.standfirst: População pode enviar sugestões até 1º de dezembro; audiência pública presencial está marcada para 8 de dezembro, com local ainda a ser definido.
articles.summary: O Plano de Gestão da Orla de Natal recebe sugestões da população pelo site da prefeitura até dezembro, com audiência pública presencial marcada para o dia 8.
articles.body:
Praia do Meio, em Natal, Rio Grande do Norte — Foto: Sérgio Henrique Santos/Inter TV Cabugi/ARQUIVO

A Prefeitura de Natal abriu uma consulta pública sobre as propostas do Plano de Gestão Integrada da Orla (PGI) e do regimento interno da audiência pública que vai discutir o documento. A população pode enviar sugestões até 1º de dezembro de 2026.

As minutas estão disponíveis para consulta e participação no site da Prefeitura . A proposta é permitir que moradores e demais interessados conheçam o conteúdo e apresentem contribuições antes da discussão pública.

O plano será debatido em uma audiência pública presencial marcada para 8 de dezembro. O local ainda será divulgado pela Prefeitura no site oficial e no Diário Oficial do Município.

O regimento interno também está aberto a contribuições. O documento estabelece as regras propostas para a organização e a realização da audiência.

O Plano de Gestão Integrada da Orla faz parte do Projeto Orla, metodologia de planejamento que busca articular políticas públicas para o ordenamento e a gestão dos espaços costeiros.

articles.title: Sorocaba confirma três casos de mpox e investiga um registro suspeito | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados da Secretaria da Saúde do município apontam que 16 suspeitas da doença infecciosa foram descartados após averiguação e que não houve mortes no período.
articles.summary: Sorocaba tem três confirmados de mpox em 2026, de acordo com dados divulgados pela Secretaria da Saúde do Estado de São Paulo. O município ainda investiga um caso suspeito.
articles.body:
Dos três casos de mpox confirmados em Sorocaba (SP), dois são em homens entre 30 e 39 anos — Foto: Reprodução

Sorocaba (SP) tem três confirmados de mpox em 2026, de acordo com dados divulgados pela Secretaria da Saúde do Estado de São Paulo (SES-SP). A Secretaria da Saúde do município informou que ainda investiga um caso e outras 16 suspeitas foram descartadas. Não há registros de mortes.

Segundo o painel do Núcleo de Informações Estratégicas em Saúde (NIES), dos casos confirmados, dois deles são em homens na faixa entre 30 e 39 anos. A terceira confirmação é em uma mulher, que tem entre 20 e 24 anos.

Segundo a secretaria municipal, os casos confirmados são importados e os pacientes em questão apenas residem em Sorocaba.

Ainda conforme os dados do NIES, todos os pacientes diagnosticados com a doença no município tiveram, entre os sintomas, lesão na pele, febre e dor muscular.

Em relação às lesões, a maior incidência foi constatada nas regiões genitais, mas também em outras áreas do corpo, como tronco, membros inferiores e palma das mãos.

A secretaria municipal explicou que o monitoramento e isolamento devem ser feitos por 21 dias, até a cura das lesões ou em caso de confirmação de resultado negativo.

Em todo o estado, 298 casos da doença já foram confirmados em 2026. A SES-SP informou que segue fazendo o monitoramento das notificações, exames laboratoriais e rastreamento de contatos para identificar possíveis cadeias de transmissão.

A mpox é uma doença infecciosa causada pelo vírus MPXV. A transmissão ocorre entre pessoas e, principalmente, pelo contato direto com lesões na pele, mucosas e secreções, inclusive durante relações sexuais.

De acordo com a SES-SP, o compartilhamento de objetos contaminados, como roupas de cama, toalhas e itens de uso pessoal também pode transmitir o vírus.

Para frear as infecções, a secretaria orienta evitar contato próximo ou íntimo com pessoas que apresentem sintomas suspeitos, não compartilhar objetos pessoais e higienizar as mãos com água e sabão ou álcool em gel.

Pessoas com suspeita da doença devem procurar atendimento de saúde e evitar contato próximo com outras pessoas. Em casos confirmados, é preciso seguir as orientações médicas de isolamento até o término do período de transmissão.

A vacinação contra a mpox é direcionada a grupos prioritários, como pessoas com HIV/Aids, usuários da profilaxia pré-exposição ao HIV (PrEP) e profissionais de laboratório com exposição ao vírus.

A SES-SP afirmou que a vacinação estratégica é ampliada gradativamente, conforme a disponibilidade de doses pelo Ministério da Saúde, e a distribuição aos municípios considera a população elegível e o cenário epidemiológico de cada região.

articles.title: Irmã de Deolane Bezerra incentiva fãs a enviarem cartas a presídio | G1
articles.standfirst: Em vídeo nas redes sociais, Daniele Bezerra explicou que a advogada recebe as correspondências enviadas à penitenciária de Tupi Paulista (SP). Influenciadora está presa preventivamente desde maio, no âmbito da Operação Vérnix.
articles.summary: A irmã da advogada e influenciadora Deolane Bezerra incentivou os seguidores a enviarem cartas à familiar, que está presa na Penitenciária Feminina de Tupi Paulista (SP).
articles.body:
Daniele Bezerra, irmã da advogada e influenciadora Deolane Bezerra , incentivou os seguidores a enviarem cartas para a Penitenciária Feminina de Tupi Paulista (SP), onde a familiar está presa desde maio, por suspeita de envolvimento em esquema de lavagem de dinheiro para o Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC).

Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, ela explicou que Deolane recebe e lê todas as mensagens e também as guarda. Confira no vídeo.

Segundo Daniele, a influenciadora recebeu telegramas com mensagens de aniversário, carinho e orações. Ela também contou que outras pessoas demonstraram preocupação por não saberem se as correspondências chegavam até Deolane.

Irmã de Deolane Bezerra (à esq.), Daniele (dir.) incentiva fãs a enviarem cartas à influenciadora presa em Tupi Paulista (SP) — Foto: Arquivo e Redes sociais/Reprodução

"Ela está recebendo todos os telegramas, todas as cartas. A unidade [prisional] entrega, ela lê e guarda com muito carinho, até o dia que ela possa trazê-los aqui para fora", informou.

Daniele ainda esclareceu que não é necessário enviar telegramas, que costumam ter um custo mais alto. De acordo com ela, as cartas convencionais também são entregues à unidade prisional, mas demoram um pouco mais para chegar.

"A diferença entre a carta e o telegrama, é porque o telegrama chega mais rápido, no outro dia, no máximo dois dias, a unidade já entrega. Porém, as cartas também são entregues. A diferença é que as cartas demoram um pouco mais para chegar até a penitenciária", explicou.

Deolane Bezerra é presa acusada de lavar dinheiro para o PCC; — Foto: Reprodução

Correspondências nas unidades prisionais

Desse total, 539.818 foram correspondências enviadas por pessoas privadas de liberdade, enquanto 431.769 foram recebidas . A coordenadoria reúne 36 complexos e unidades prisionais, dos quais o presídio de Tupi Paulista faz parte.

Em 2025, foram registradas 625.345 correspondências enviadas e 512.400 recebidas . Já em 2024, os números foram de 637.978 e 530.957 , respectivamente.

Segundo a Secretaria da Administração Penitenciária (SAP), as correspondências passam por procedimentos de segurança.

As cartas são recebidas pela portaria e pela área de segurança, que verificam a identificação de remetentes e destinatários e realizam inspeções físicas. Caso sejam identificadas irregularidades, podem ser adotadas medidas administrativas.

Deolane Bezerra escreveu carta da penitenciária — Foto: Reprodução

No fim de agosto, a Justiça decidiu manter a advogada e os demais réus presos . Na época, a defesa de Deolane classificou a decisão como “desnecessária, ilegal e desproporcional”.

Segundo a denúncia do Ministério Público, a organização criminosa era dividida em três núcleos: o decisório, integrado pelo chefe do PCC, Marco Willians Herbas Camacho , e Alejandro Juvenal Herbas Camacho Junior ; o operacional; e o financeiro - segundo a acusação, Deolane integra esse último grupo.

Os promotores do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco) afirmam que Deolane seria " a principal integrante do núcleo financeiro , responsável por ocultar e dissimular recursos de origem ilícita por meio de contas bancárias vinculadas a ela e às suas empresas, além de converter esses valores em bens de alto valor econômico".

Outro argumento apresentado pelo Gaeco é que dois dos denunciados, Paloma Sanches Herbas Camacho e Leonardo Alexsander Ribeiro Herbas Camacho, continuam foragidos, o que, na avaliação da Promotoria, reforça a necessidade da prisão preventiva para assegurar a aplicação da lei penal.

A defesa de Deolane Bezerra alega que a cliente é inocente e que não possui vínculos com a organização criminosa.

Deolane Bezerra foi transferida para a Penitenciária Feminina de Tupi Paulista, no oeste paulista — Foto: Reprodução/Delolane Bezerra/Instagram - Divulgação/SAP

Segundo a denúncia, os investigados integrariam uma organização criminosa voltada à ocultação e à dissimulação de recursos provenientes de atividades ilícitas atribuídas ao PCC.

De acordo com o Ministério Público, análises de documentos fiscais, bancários e relatórios técnicos apontariam movimentações de grandes quantias de dinheiro e a conversão desses recursos em ativos com aparência de origem legal. A acusação sustenta ainda que o grupo utilizava empresas de fachada e pessoas interpostas, conhecidas como "laranjas", para esconder a origem do dinheiro.

Em julho, o Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo (TJ-SP) negou, por unanimidade, um pedido de habeas corpus apresentado pela defesa de Deolane . Na ocasião, a relatora, desembargadora Renata Cantello, afirmou que as alegações apresentadas pela defesa e por relatório da OAB-SP representavam "meras insatisfações com a rigidez natural do regime de reclusão e questões de gestão administrativa interna", sem demonstrar ilegalidade na prisão preventiva nem justificar sua substituição por prisão domiciliar.

Deolane Bezerra chega à Penitenciária de Tupi Paulista (SP) — Foto: Aceituno Jr./TV TEM

Naquele momento, a defesa de Deolane Bezerra diz que recebe a decisão de manutenção da prisão preventiva com surpresa, já que a prisão é manifestamente desnecessária, ilegal e desproporcional.

Informa que sua cliente é inocente, não possuindo vínculo nenhum com organização criminosa, e que sua movimentação financeira é decorrente de atividades empresariais lícitas e de honorários advocatícios, conforme será devidamente comprovado durante a instrução probatória.

A defesa reitera sua confiança nas instituições e continuará adotando todos os instrumentos cabíveis para restabelecer a liberdade.

articles.title: Why is Paraguay facing a banking and political crisis?
articles.summary: Ueno collapse raises questions about state influence and accountability.
articles.body:
Paraguay is engulfed in political turmoil after a banking scandal put its president and major institutions under scrutiny.

At the centre is Ueno, a fast-growing digital lender, whose collapse has left millions of people unable to access their savings. But the fallout goes beyond the banking sector.

Congress has rejected President Santiago Pena’s resignation and is pressing ahead with impeachment proceedings. He’s accused of negligence and being complicit in an alleged cover-up of the bank’s insolvency.

So, what went wrong? Were regulators compromised by political influence? And who should be held accountable?

Daniel Duarte Braga – Journalist and contributing editor to The Paraguay Post

Mariano Machado – Principal Americas analyst at global risk intelligence firm, Verisk Maplecroft

Javier Farje – Historian specialising in Latin American affairs

articles.title: Nenhum detento é recapturado um mês após fuga em massa no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Oito presos escaparam da Unidade Penal Moacir Prado, em Tarauacá, no dia 5 de outubro, após abrirem um buraco na estrutura de uma das celas.
articles.summary: Oito presos escaparam da Unidade Penal Moacir Prado, em Tarauacá, no dia 5 de outubro, após abrirem um buraco na estrutura de uma das celas.
articles.body:
Oito detentos fugiram do presídio de Tarauacá no dia 5 de outubro — Foto: Arquivo/Iapen-AC

Mais de um mês após a fuga em massa de oito detentos da Unidade Penal Moacir Prado , em Tarauacá , no interior do Acre, nenhum deles ainda foi recapturado.

A informação foi confirmada ao g1 nesta sexta-feira (6) pelo Instituto de Administração Penitenciária do Acre (Iapen-AC), que também informou que as buscas pelos fugitivos continuam.

Os presos fugiram no dia 5 de outubro, depois de abrirem um buraco na estrutura de uma das celas do presídio. Entre os oito fugitivos, seis têm condenação e cumprem pena.

A fuga foi constatada durante uma inspeção de rotina na unidade prisional. Na ocasião, a direção identificou uma violação na estrutura de uma das celas e, após conferir os internos, percebeu a ausência dos oito detentos.

À época, o Iapen informou que os protocolos de segurança foram acionados assim que a fuga foi identificada. Equipes da Polícia Penal de Cruzeiro do Sul também foram deslocadas para reforçar as buscas na região.

Conforme o Iapen, as equipes enfrentam dificuldades para chegar aos locais onde os fugitivos poderiam estar escondidos.

Detentos fizeram buraco em cela e fugiram de presídio em Tarauacá no dia 5 de outubro — Foto: Arquivo/Iapen-AC

A principal dificuldade é o acesso aos ramais da região, para onde os detentos teriam seguido após deixar a unidade prisional. A suspeita é de que a maioria dos fugitivos está escondida em áreas de mata.

articles.title: Acidente de lancha em Novo Airão: barco colide no Rio Negro | G1
articles.standfirst: Embarcação seguia de São Gabriel da Cachoeira para Manaus quando colidiu contra a margem do rio Negro, em trecho conhecido como Paraná do Jacaré, nas proximidades de Novo Airão.
articles.summary: Acidente de lancha em Novo Airão foi causado por fumaça e seca no Rio Negro; passageiros da Expresso Dedé foram resgatados e seguiram viagem para Manaus.
articles.body:
Uma lancha da empresa Expresso Dedé colidiu contra um barranco nesta sexta-feira (6), nas proximidades de Novo Airão , no interior do Amazonas. A embarcação fazia a rota entre São Gabriel da Cachoeira e Manaus e navegava pelo rio Negro, em um trecho conhecido como Paraná do Jacaré.

Apesar do susto, não há registro de ferimentos ou mortes.

Segundo a Defesa Civil de Novo Airão, o condutor da lancha afirmou que a fumaça na região reduziu a visibilidade e contribuiu para o acidente. Ainda de acordo com a Defesa Civil, as condições de navegabilidade do rio também estavam prejudicadas pela estiagem.

Conforme relatos de testemunhas, o impacto danificou a parte frontal da lancha, o que causou pânico entre os passageiros. Eles foram retirados com a ajuda de moradores e outros navegantes que estavam nas proximidades.

A Defesa Civil foi ao local e resgatou passageiros e tripulantes, que já estavam em terra firme. Em seguida, todos foram transferidos para outra embarcação, que seguiu viagem até Manaus.

Lancha colidiu contra barranco na margem do rio. De acordo com a Defesa Civil, a fumaça presente no local e a estiagem no rio Negro contribuíram para o acidente. — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil de Novo Airão

articles.title: Mega GWM chega a Vilhena (RO) com inauguração de showroom no dia 7 de novembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Espaço no centro da cidade marca a chegada do Grupo Gilberto Miranda ao Cone Sul de Rondônia e apresenta sua linha de veículos multienergia.
articles.summary: Espaço no centro da cidade marca a chegada do Grupo Gilberto Miranda ao Cone Sul de Rondônia e apresenta sua linha de veículos multienergia.
articles.body:
House Of Tomorrow em Vilhena (RO) — Foto: Divulgação

A Mega GWM , do Grupo Gilberto Miranda, está ampliando sua presença de mercado em Rondônia. Desta vez, a expansão chega a Vilhena, no Cone Sul do estado, com a inauguração de uma unidade da House of Tomorrow, marcada para sábado (07), às 09h . O evento de inauguração será aberto ao público.

A nova unidade representa um investimento no município e deve contribuir para a economia local, com geração de empregos, novas oportunidades e movimentação do comércio. A chegada também demonstra a aposta do grupo no potencial de crescimento de Vilhena e das cidades do Cone Sul.

Com o showroom, os consumidores da região poderão conhecer os veículos da GWM, receber atendimento especializado e realizar negociações sem precisar se deslocar para outras cidades.

A marca oferece veículos híbridos, elétricos e a combustão, com tecnologias voltadas à eficiência, ao desempenho e à inovação. O espaço da House of Tomorrow em Vilhena, foi pensado para apresentar esse conceito de mobilidade em um ambiente moderno, permitindo que os visitantes conheçam de perto os modelos e os diferenciais da fabricante.

A inauguração será realizada no sábado (07), a partir das 09h, na Rua Osvaldo Cruz, nº 233, no Centro de Vilhena . O evento terá entrada gratuita e será aberto ao público.

articles.title: Caged: Acre fecha setembro com saldo positivo de 235 contratações | G1
articles.standfirst: Apesar do saldo positivo, volume foi 41,25% menor do que em agosto. Setor de serviços liderou a geração de empregos, registrando 347 novas vagas.
articles.summary: Apesar de manter resultado positivo pelo 8º mês seguido, volume foi 41,25% menor do que em agosto. Setor de serviços liderou a geração de empregos, registrando 347 novas vagas.
articles.body:
O mês de setembro foi o oitavo seguido deste ano no qual o Acre encerrou com saldo positivo na geração de empregos, segundo o Novo Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged). Foram criados 235 postos , resultado de 4.468 admissões e 4.413 desligamentos naquele mês.

Contudo, o volume foi 41,25% menor que o de agosto, que foi de 400 vagas , e o menor índice do ano entre os saldos positivos. Ainda assim, o estado segue com somente o mês de janeiro com saldo negativo.

Mais uma vez, o setor de maior destaque foi o de serviços , com saldo positivo de 347 vagas. A indústria se recuperou do agosto negativo, e registrou saldo de 3 vagas em setembro.

O comércio também terminou o período no positivo, com 50 vagas.

Oito dos nove meses do ano com resultado já divulgado tiveram saldo positivo na geração de emprego no Acre — Foto: Emely Azevedo/Seict

Assim como no mês passado, duas áreas tiveram mais demissões que contratações: construção , que alcançou o pior saldo no recorte, com perda de 96 vagas, e a agropecuária , que ficou com saldo negativo de 69 postos. O primeiro setor já havia acumulado queda em agosto, quando perdeu 20 vagas.

Com estes números, o estoque mensal de trabalhadores, ou seja, quantidade de pessoas que atuam em vagas formais, ficou em 113.304.

articles.title: Alerta vermelho em SC: tempestades ameaçam cidades atingidas | G1
articles.standfirst: Órgão alerta para risco muito alto de vendavais, granizo e chuva intensa. Período mais crítico deve ser entre a madrugada e a manhã de sábado (7).
articles.summary: Órgão alerta para risco muito alto de vendavais, granizo e chuva intensa. Período mais crítico deve ser entre a madrugada e a manhã de sábado (7).
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil emitiu nesta sexta-feira (6) um aviso de risco alto a muito alto para a ocorrência de vendavais, queda de granizo e chuva intensa no Oeste de Santa Catarina . A região foi atingida nesta semana por dois tornados que provocaram estragos e deixaram mais de 500 pessoas desalojadas.

🔴 O aviso especial vermelho indica risco muito alto para ocorrências associadas aos temporais, como destelhamentos , danos à rede elétrica , queda de galhos e árvores, alagamentos e enxurradas pontuais.

O período de maior preocupação é a madrugada e a manhã de sábado (7), quando a formação de uma frente fria deve intensificar as instabilidades.

Inicialmente, as instabilidades devem ocorrer de forma localizada, acompanhadas de raios, rajadas de vento e eventual queda de granizo, devido à combinação de calor, umidade e áreas de baixa pressão.

Já na madrugada e manhã de sábado, as tempestades podem ganhar força, especialmente na região Oeste. Segundo a Defesa Civil, as rajadas de vento podem ultrapassar 80 km/h.

➡️ Além dos ventos fortes, a chuva prevista para o fim de semana aumenta o risco de alagamentos e enxurradas no Oeste, principalmente em áreas próximas a rios menores. O risco de deslizamentos também é alto nessas regiões e no Vale do Itajaí. A preocupação está relacionada ao solo já encharcado pelas chuvas registradas nos últimos dias.

Nas demais áreas de Santa Catarina, também há risco alto de temporais ao longo da manhã, porém, em menor intensidade.

Imagens aéreas mostram dimensão dos estragos após tornado devastar cidade de SC — Foto: @dechapeco/divulgação

Durante os temporais busque um local abrigado, longe de janelas e objetos que possam ser arremessados.

Em caso de ventos fortes evite transitar e/ou abrigar-se próximo de árvores, placas, muros e postes de energia.

articles.title: California family wins $8 million after neighbour calls autistic boy a ‘public nuisance’ over backyard noises; neighbour asked if there's a cure for his autism; mother says lawsuit forced them to leave their home
articles.summary: A Northern California family has been awarded $8 million after a prolonged legal battle with their next-door neighbour, who sued them over the backyard
articles.body: A Northern California family has been awarded $8 million after a prolonged legal battle with their next-door neighbour, who sued them over the backyard noises made by their autistic son, describing him as a ‘public nuisance’. The case, which was heard in Santa Clara County, involved Ezequiel Arvayo, his mother Serena Arvayo and a neighbour who alleged that the child's vocal outbursts disrupted her daily life, affected her work and caused emotional distress.According to reports by NBC Bay Area and KRON4, the dispute began when the neighbour filed a lawsuit against the family and their landlord in December 2023. However, the family challenged the allegations through a countersuit, and a jury eventually awarded them $8 million for intentional infliction of emotional distress.Why did the neighbour sue the family over their autistic son's backyard noises?Ezequiel, his mother and his grandfather were living in a rented house on Boynton Avenue in San Jose, California, when their neighbour initiated legal proceedings against them. In her December 2023 complaint, she sought a public nuisance abatement and a restraining order, alleging that the boy's behaviour was disruptive.As per reports, the neighbour described the child's behaviour as ‘indecent’ and ‘offensive’. She alleged that he was left in the backyard daily, where he would ‘wail and scream for hours, often without adult supervision’.She further claimed that the noises caused emotional distress, interfered with her work-from-home arrangements, affected her career and business, and deprived her of the enjoyment of her property.Family explains why the autistic boy made noises in the backyardThe family's lawyers challenged the allegations in a cross-complaint filed in March 2024. They explained that Ezequiel is nonverbal and has Level 3 autism, a condition he was diagnosed with at the age of two.According to the legal filing, the boy faces significant communication and sensory challenges and requires round-the-clock supervision. His mother, Serena, is a single parent who has dedicated her life to caring for him.The family also explained that Ezequiel attends school and behavioural therapy every weekday from 8 am to 6 pm. During weekend afternoons, he enjoys chasing bubbles in the backyard. These activities sometimes lead him to express happiness through vocal stimming, a form of self-stimulatory behaviour involving vocalisations.The family's lawyers maintained that he was never left unsupervised and that the sounds were an expression of his emotions rather than deliberate attempts to disturb anyone.Neighbour allegedly asked if there was a cure for the boy's autismThe family's cross-complaint also described an alleged confrontation between Serena and the neighbour before the lawsuit was filed.According to the filing, the neighbour complained about Ezequiel and asked that he no longer be allowed to play in the backyard. Serena reportedly tried to explain that her son was nonverbal and had a severe form of autism, making the noises an uncontrollable way for him to express his emotions.The lawyers further alleged that the neighbour asked Serena whether there was a cure for her son's condition, directly in front of the child.Court records also reportedly included text messages in which the neighbour complained to the family's landlord about Ezequiel making ‘strange noises’.Jury awards the family $8 million in emotional distress caseThe legal battle eventually went before a jury in Santa Clara County. According to the family's attorneys, the jury awarded Ezequiel and his family $8 million for intentional infliction of emotional distress.Speaking about the impact of the dispute, Serena said the experience had been deeply hurtful and that describing her son as a nuisance had affected his dignity.“My son was represented with dignity, and that was the most important thing for him, to have the dignity he deserves,” she told NBC Bay Area.Her legal representatives also welcomed the verdict. Attorney Rachael Boden, speaking to KRON4, described the outcome as a significant moment of justice for the family. She said the jury had understood their struggles and hoped the case would encourage greater empathy towards families raising children with autism.The neighbour's attorney did not immediately respond to media requests for comment.Family moved out of their home following the disputeThe legal battle also affected the family's living arrangements. As reported by KRON4 and NBC Bay Area, Serena and Ezequiel eventually moved out of the Boynton Avenue rental property following the dispute, although the neighbour's legal action continued.The move reportedly meant that the family had to deal with higher rent at their new home.Serena's lawyers said the $8 million award would help provide Ezequiel with the assistance and financial security he needs in the future.You use AI every day. articles.title: Spate of bomb threats poses serious challenge to airline industry
articles.summary: After a week of disruption, airlines are facing both safety and financial concerns.
articles.body:
With no fewer than 32 bomb threats affecting a dozen airlines in the space of four days, the aviation industry is facing another potential crisis.

Some of the threats apparently came from phone calls, others via email, and although they have all turned out to be hoaxes, they were each clearly serious enough to force emergency action.

Some planes had to be escorted by military jets, others were quietly inspected mid-air by cabin crew - desperate not to cause alarm.

A number had to be re-routed from their original destinations, landing at different airports, sometimes in different countries. An Aer Lingus flight had to land at an airbase 1,000 kilometers from its intended destination after running low on fuel.

New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines

All this poses a serious challenge to the airlines, who have little idea who is causing the severe disruption they have faced almost every day this week.

Although so far all threats have turned out to be hoaxes, airlines have no choice but take each threat seriously.

"They have a triage system, but follow the same protocols for each until they are absolutely sure there is no threat," says Marco Chan, a former commercial airline pilot and aviation expert at Kingston University.

"That could involve a mid-air inspection, but definitely a search once the plane has landed.

"Passengers might not even know there is an issue until they are told to disembark. It can cause disruption, but that is a small price to pay when safety is at stake", he adds.

The sight of sniffer dogs and specialist teams on the tarmac searching for explosives on commercial planes may cause alarm.

So far, the disruption too has been limited to the few thousand passengers who have been directly involved.

Paul Mason, an aviation security expert, says there will be a financial cost to the airline involved, but planes get diverted every day.

"The number can sometimes run to over a hundred planes daily, for things like technical issues, medical emergencies, even the weather," he adds. "They far outweigh the few which have been diverted due to hoaxes. So airlines are well equipped at dealing with the unexpected."

It is also unlikely that customers will be able to get refunds, he explains, because these incidents are not the fault of the airlines.

The more worrying aspect over the past few days will be the seeming random nature of the targets and the lack of any credible intelligence regarding who is behind the threats.

Aside from emails suggesting that an extremist misogynist group had claimed responsibility for a handful of the incidents - although since denied by its founder - there appear to be few leads.

With 20 years of military experience as well, Paul Mason says the incidents bear the hallmarks of hybrid warfare, which involves unconventional methods such as cyber attacks.

"It does feel co-ordinated," he says. "Russia has said it's got nothing to do with it, but it could be proxies. It's a very easy way to create disruption and chaos, with plausible deniability."

"That's the problem. Someone can have an opinion on who is behind it, but if the perpetrators are using sophisticated technology, it will be very hard to trace them."

He does say however that if misguided individuals try to copy the threats they could find themselves in serious trouble.

The Aviation Security Act 1982 states that "intentionally communicating false, misleading, or deceptive information that endangers - or is likely to endanger - the safety of an aircraft in flight is a serious criminal offense".

The maximum sentence is life imprisonment.

There is precious little that airports and airlines can do to guard against actually receiving threats, as they can come from a vast range of sources. But the punishment is designed to act as a deterrent.

As Paul Mason warns: "Someone might think it's a laugh and very easy to do, but unless they are very sophisticated, they are highly likely to be traced. And find themselves facing prison."

articles.title: Taiwan to close representative office in Papua New Guinea, blames China
articles.summary: Amid the fallout, Taiwan says it will stop purchases of liquefied natural gas from Port Moresby.
articles.body:
Taiwan says it is closing its representative office in Papua New Guinea and will stop buying liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the country, blaming Chinese political pressure on the South Pacific nation.

Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Friday that Papua New Guinea had repeated previous demands that staff leave its office in the capital, Port Moresby, within a set deadline and had pushed for ⁠its closure.

These actions “reflect China’s continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in other countries’ diplomatic decisions and suppress Taiwan’s international space”, it said in a statement.

China, which claims Taiwan as part of its territory, had welcomed Papua New Guinea’s decision in July to shutter Taiwan’s office in Port Moresby. Taipei rejected the move, and the office remained open in the interim.

The Pacific has long been an area for diplomatic competition between China and Taiwan. Papua New Guinea has formal diplomatic relations with China, but it had allowed Taiwan to have a representative office in Port Moresby.

Taiwan has formal diplomatic ties with only three Pacific Islands nations: Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands. It also has a representative office in Fiji. Just 12 countries maintain formal ⁠diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

Taiwan previously announced that it had stopped spot purchases of LNG from the South Pacific nation, but on Friday the ministry said it also would no longer sign new spot purchase contracts with the country.

Taiwanese LNG purchases accounted for one-third of Papua New Guinea’s exports.

Last year, Taiwan imported about 8 percent of its natural gas from Port Moresby.

Taipei will also end technical cooperation and assistance programmes, “including medical missions, related scholarship and talent development programmes”, the ministry said.

articles.title: Goole food bank to close amid rising costs and drop in donations
articles.summary: A food bank in Goole annouces it will close in January as costs rise and donations drop.
articles.body:
A food bank serving an East Yorkshire town has closed after 16 years due to rising costs and a drop in donations.

The Mission Trinity Food Bank, which supports people in Goole and the surrounding villages, began as part of the local Methodist church's mission to help homeless people and those facing financial hardship.

Founder David Sample said: "Over time our funds have declined and declined, to the point where we can't really afford to keep going much longer, and also because of this cost of living crisis that's going on at the moment."

He said the charity was buying in food up to three times a week to keep up with demand despite a drop in donations.

"We've had to go out and buy more food with our funds, so we've been spending an awful lot more just to keep the basics in," he said.

He said personal circumstances had also incluenced the decision.

Sample was originally employed by the church to run the food bank, but since being made redundant he has been running it as a volunteer.

The food bank, which supports about 50-60 families and individuals each week, will continue to run until January.

Sample described his time at the food bank as a "rollercoaster", and said he had some "stressful times" as well as some times when he encountered heart-warming moments.

He said: "We've encountered people struggling with grief and their world falling in around about them, and they've come to us for help.

"We've done what we do and a couple of years later, they've been back and brought us stuff, so it's been very good that way."

Sample thanked all the "unbelievable" volunteers who have supported the food bank over the years.

He said he would be "happy" if someone came forward to take on the food bank, but they would need to find new funding streams to keep operating the project.

articles.title: Under-16s could be banned from buying energy drinks in Wales
articles.summary: Young people in Cardiff told BBC Wales they supported the proposed ban.
articles.body:
Young people and experts say they support the Welsh government's plan to ban children under 16 from buying high-caffeine energy drinks.

The Welsh government said that evidence suggests a link between "consumption of high-caffeine energy drinks and negative health outcomes", and is considering a ban on under 16s buying them.

BBC Wales spoke to young people in Cardiff who said they supported the proposed ban, with one 17-year-old saying it was "really easy to start relying on them".

The British Soft Drinks Association said the proposed ban was "unnecessary and not supported by robust evidence of overconsumption or harm".

The news follows the ban in England where drinks like Red Bull, Monster, Relentless and Prime will be illegal to sell to under-16s from April, aimed at reducing obesity levels, disrupted sleep and anxiety.

Any drink containing more than 150mg of caffeine per litre will be illegal to sell to children and younger teenagers in shops, restaurants, cafes, vending machines and online from next April in England.

Lower-caffeine soft drinks, such Diet Coke, as well as tea and coffee are not affected.

Excessive caffeine consumption has been linked to headaches and sleep problems , and experts say young people can be more sensitive to caffeine as they have smaller bodies and their brains are still developing.

Some popular drinks brands contain more caffeine than two cups of coffee or four cans of cola.

Vee, 17, from Cardiff, said she was happy about the proposed ban, while Sunny, 16, urged people to "just have a coffee" instead of an energy drink.

Too much caffeine can cause a rapid heart rate, abnormal heart rhythms and seizures, and although rare, there have been some deaths linked to excess caffeine .

The sugary versions of the drinks can also contribute to obesity and damaged teeth, according to the Association of UK Dieticians.

Currently any drink, other than tea or coffee, with over 150mg requires a label warning of its high caffeine content that says it is not recommended for children or pregnant or breast-feeding women.

For most adults, up to 400mg of caffeine a day, or about four cups of instant coffee or five cups of tea, is safe.

Aisling Pigott, a nutritionist and registered dietician in Cardiff, said she was pleased to hear of the proposed ban but that it was probably "10 years too late".

She said Wales has "disproportionate concerns around diet and lifestyle" and while this would not be a "magic bullet", it was a "step in the right direction".

Pigott described caffeine as "a bit like going into your overdraft - you might immediately have a little bit more money or cash, but that does need to be repaid in some format".

She said someone may have a little more concentration, but that is "followed by a crash".

"Because I'm a dietitian, my concern around excessive consumption of these drinks also sits with what what are they not consuming when they're drinking?

"I see and hear a lot of children and young people drinking these drinks instead of food, so using the sugar and caffeine as an easier access to give energy than really nutritious, healthy, balanced diet."

In a written statement, Public and Preventative Health Minister Nerys Evans said the latest evidence suggested a link between consumption of high-caffeine energy drinks and negative health outcomes in children.

"This includes increased frequency of headaches, irritation, tiredness and stomach aches, reduced sleep duration and quality and increased risk of stress, anxiety and depression," she said.

"The previous Welsh government consulted and gathered evidence on proposals to restrict the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to children under 16, with broad support for action."

Evans added: "Having considered the evidence and responses to that earlier consultation, the current Welsh government intends to take forward proposals to prohibit the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to children under 16, subject to the outcome of this consultation.

"These are drinks, other than tea or coffee, that contain over 150mg of caffeine per litre."

The Welsh government said the consultation would seek views on the proposed "enforcement framework", including "online age-verification arrangements, assessing compliance activity, sanctions, implementation timescales and monitoring arrangements".

British Soft Drinks Association said its members have not marketed or promoted the sale of energy drinks to under-16s since 2010.

"All high-caffeine beverages carry a 'not recommended for children' label. The available evidence shows that the vast majority of caffeine consumed by children and adolescents comes from sources other than energy drinks."

articles.title: Jersey cyber boss warns over tech vulnerabilities
articles.summary: The Jersey Cyber Security Centre boss is "challenging whether everyone needs a connected fridge".
articles.body:
The boss of the island's cyber security centre has questioned whether so many household and commercial appliances need to be connected to the internet.

It comes after dozens of European supermarkets were hit by cyber-attacks that increased the temperature of freezers to more than 50C (122F).

Matt Palmer, the director of the Jersey Cyber Security Centre, said he "wasn't suggesting that people should unplug devices, but that he would challenge whether everyone needs a connected fridge".

Mark Cox, the chief executive of CI Coop, said its supermarkets had security controls in place in case of cyber threats.

Smart devices connected to the internet can include fridges, central heating and even toasters and washing machines.

There is no evidence domestic appliances are being targeted in the cyber-attacks which affected supermarkets, but it raised questions about the extent to which smart devices are routinely linked to the internet .

Palmer said the field was not easily understood or considered by people.

"It's like it doesn't really exist until it happens to you... this is happening now, all the time, every single day and therefore any system that is connected to the internet, it is only a matter of time until someone finds a way to compromise it if it's vulnerable," he said.

"Which is why it's incredibly important that we patch devices quickly and we only connect devices to the internet if we really need to do so."

He explained his team had three computers around the world that serve as "honey pots" with the aim of appearing vulnerable to attack from hackers.

"Some of those vulnerabilities won't be in a honey pot... they will be in the real systems that we depend on every day, for our lives, for our work, for our families," he said.

"You will see these sudden bursts of attack, that does happen all the time, it can be quiet, it can be busy but it's a constant pulse of activity by people around the internet scanning the systems to see if they are vulnerable."

A spate of cyber-attacks in recent weeks affected supermarkets across Europe as well as the UK meat industry and blood stores in France .

The CI Coop boss said it took cyber-security "extremely seriously" and it was monitoring the European situation closely.

"We are carrying out a specific review of our refrigeration and freezer systems, including their connectivity and the arrangements we have in place with relevant suppliers and service partners" Cox said.

"We also have established procedures for monitoring refrigeration temperatures and protecting food safety, and we will continue to keep our systems and controls under review in light of emerging threats."

The BBC has approached other supermarkets on the island for comment.

Government of Jersey chief executive officer Paul Wylie described cyber-security as one of the island's "top risks" during a scrutiny hearing last month.

The Cyber Security Policy Framework outlined strengthening Jersey businesses' cyber-security and resilience as a top priority.

Wylie said: "We will ensure businesses, organisations and islanders understand the cyber threats they face, supporting their adoption of relevant protective measures and their recovery from a cyber-attack."

articles.title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules
articles.summary: A post-Brexit deal on food standards has raised questions over the future naming of the classic British snack.
articles.body:
The naming of smoky bacon-flavoured crisps has become the latest political headache to emerge from the government's bid for closer ties with the EU.

The government is negotiating a deal on food standards in a bid to cut costs for British companies trading with Europe.

Labour ministers have been keen to talk up the potential economic benefits of the agreement, which could be announced at a summit later this month.

But the deal's requirement for Britain to adopt EU food rules in a wide range of areas has threatened to reignite sovereignty debates from the Brexit era.

Labour ministers have been keen to sidestep talking about the impact of alignment in particular sectors, instead stressing the overall economic boost it expects the food deal to bring.

On Thursday, Environment Secretary Angela Eagle told a radio presenter he should "get a life" when he asked about the potential impact of the new rules on snacks, such as smoky bacon crisps.

But it highlights the political dangers for the government of realigning with regulations that British politicians have not been able to shape, with the Conservatives and Reform UK keen to pounce on cases showing Britain to be a "rule taker" from Brussels.

It is not the first regulatory skirmish over smoky bacon crisps - following previous headlines over how the well-loved British flavour could be affected by an EU decision in 2024 to phase out a number of artificial smoke flavourings.

Now, the flavour name itself has been called into question by a separate EU attempt to restrict how descriptions of meat are used to market food.

Under rules adopted this summer, the EU plans to restrict the use of 31 terms, including bacon, drumstick and steak, to products that contain meat, claiming consumers could be confused by plant-based alternatives using the same names.

The European snack industry is seeking clarity on how the rules, which will also cover terms such as pork, chicken and beef, would apply to meat-flavoured crisps, including those flavoured without the use of any meat extracts.

The UK government has said it expects the new regulations to be in scope of its proposed food standards deal.

This means they would also apply to companies marketing their products in Britain, which is among the biggest consumers of crisps in Europe, according to analysts Euromonitor.

It has raised the prospect that crisps with names such as smoky bacon and roast chicken could have to be relabelled to be sold in British shops, although much remains unclear about how the rules will apply in practice.

The new EU rules, which will not come into force until after August 2029, will allow the European Commission to create exemptions for meaty names with an established long-term use to describe other types of food product.

The Brussels-based body is yet to set out how it plans to use this power, or what it means for snacks.

A group of conservative German MEPs are also seeking a specific carve-out for meat names in snacks and sauces in separate legislation currently making its way through the European Parliament.

The Food and Drink Federation, which represents British crispmakers including Walkers and KP Snacks, has been supportive of the government's bid to reach a food deal due to its potential to reduce trade barriers with Europe.

But it has highlighted the new rules as an example of where it wants the government to work with industry to ensure UK interests are reflected in EU decision making.

"Meat protections are an example of a new EU rule that UK businesses will need to comply with, but which the UK was not involved in developing," added the body's chief scientific officer Kate Halliwell.

The Potato Processors' Association, which also represents a number of major snackmakers, said it was monitoring the situation closely and wanted to see clarification of how the rules could affect its members.

Vanessa Richardson, its deputy director general, said her association supported moves to reduce "unnecessary barriers" in the trade of food products.

But she added it was important that the government's deal is implemented in a way that "avoids unintended consequences for established product descriptions which consumers clearly understand as referring to a flavour".

The Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) says it stands ready to help British snack businesses prepare for the impact of the new EU rules.

It is not yet clear what a British version of the rules would look like, or whether they would need to apply from 2029 alongside the new European regulations.

articles.title: Fake GoFundMe collected more than $5,000 after a Massachusetts teenager died in a Florida crash; the family said the campaign was created without their permission
articles.summary: A fake GoFundMe campaign claiming to collect funeral expenses for a Massachusetts teenager killed in a Florida car crash raised thousands of dollars
articles.body: A fake GoFundMe campaign claiming to collect funeral expenses for a Massachusetts teenager killed in a Florida car crash raised thousands of dollars before it was removed from the platform in April 2025. The fundraiser was created without the permission of the victim’s family and falsely presented itself as an effort to support them following the tragedy. The incident prompted a warning from school officials, raised concerns about online fundraising during emergencies and led GoFundMe to suspend donations while it investigated the campaign.Fake GoFundMe exploit the tragedy involving Hannah WassermanThe fraudulent fundraising page appeared online shortly after three seniors from Concord-Carlisle High School in Massachusetts died in a crash during their spring break in Florida. It claimed to be raising money to help cover funeral expenses for 18-year-old Hannah Wasserman, one of the students killed in the accident.According to CBS Boston, the campaign appeared on Tuesday, April 22, 2025, and had reportedly collected more than $8,000 by Wednesday. articles.title: Pro-life display at Ohio university targeted by chilling online threat to 'Kirk the anti-abortion table'
articles.summary: A Miami University student faces a felony terroristic threat charge after allegedly posting a Yik Yak message referencing Charlie Kirk's assassination.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE – A pro-life student display at Miami University in Ohio became the target of an alarming online threat, prompting a police investigation and the felony arrest of an alleged poster, according to Students for Life of America. The incident unfolded due to an Oct. 28 Yik Yak post as the group hosted a campus display, with screenshots appearing to show a user on the anonymous social media platform asking, "How many dining dollars to Kirk the anti abortion table in Armstrong," an apparent reference to the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. "We were in the Armstrong Student Center inside," Grace Kimzey, Ohio Regional Coordinator for Students for Life of America, told Fox News Digital in an interview Friday. ‘FEMINISTS LIED’ TOUR AIMS TO CHALLENGE ABORTION, FEMINISM NARRATIVES ON COLLEGE CAMPUSES "We had our display, we were towards the end of our tabling in our tour when a student saw a post online at Yik Yak," Kimzey said. "He was just keeping tabs on what's being talked about on social media, about our table and about our display. So we saw that, and then I immediately called the Miami Police Department just to keep our students safe." A press release from Students for Life of America, shared exclusively with Fox News Digital, said that a 19-year-old Miami University student was arrested on Nov. 2, on a felony charge and multiple misdemeanor charges after allegedly posting the message on Yik Yak appearing to encourage violence against Students for Life of America members staffing the campus pro-life display. CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION ALLEGEDLY MOCKED ON CAMPUSES ACROSS COUNTRY WITH CELEBRATIONS, LOOK-ALIKE CONTESTS According to Students for Life, the post was made in Yik Yak's "Miami Ohio" group, which is visible to the app's users near the university. The group said that the student was arrested and charged with one felony of making a terroristic threat and various misdemeanors, including inducing panic, aggravated menacing, and telecommunications harassment. The incident was also referred to the FBI. Kristan Hawkins, president of Students for Life of America, told Fox News Digital in a statement that the climate for free speech has significantly deteriorated in recent years. "I've been on campuses for the past three weeks alongside Turning Point USA on my fall tour, and I'm there, you know, under a TPUSA tent. Cameras are on me. There are signs saying we are filming in this area, yet there will be students who will stand beside me and call me Mrs. Kirk, and they'll use the verb ‘Kirked’ over and over again," Hawkins said. GEORGETOWN STUDENTS PLAN CHARLIE KIRK 'LOOKALIKE CONTEST' ON ANNIVERSARY OF HIS ASSASSINATION "I've asked students just to their faces when they will say something about Charlie," Hawkins continued. "They'll laugh, I'll say, ‘Do you think it was funny what happened to my friend, that he was assassinated, a husband and a father who was a good man by all accounts? You think this was funny?’ And they'll just continue to laugh." She also recounted another recent incident with a student that gave her pause. "I asked one student recently, ‘Do you think it's moral to shoot me? If you disagree with me and what I do, do you think it's moral to shoot me?’ And the young man looked right at me and said, ‘Yes,’" Hawkins said. "I mean, this is a different level. And I think the older generations, even my generation, the elder millennials, if you will, when we were having dialogue on campuses, it didn't reach this level." UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT SOUNDS ALARM AS NEARLY HALF OF STUDENTS JUSTIFY VIOLENCE TO STOP 'HATE SPEECH' A spokesperson from Miami University told Fox News Digital in a statement that, "Due to the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), the university cannot confirm if a student is being disciplined or is currently in the disciplinary process." "Every Miami student is afforded their due process rights through our Code of Student Conduct," the spokesperson continued. "The university handles any reports of possible policy violations by students or violations of law through the Office of Community Standards and through campus and local law enforcement, with potential sanctions that vary based on the alleged violation and a student’s previous conduct history." The spokesperson referred to the university’s website for more information about freedom of speech and expression at Miami University. articles.title: Antonio Brown avoids jail by pleading guilty to lesser charge in Miami shooting
articles.summary: Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown, accused of opening fire at a man in Miami last year, pleaded guilty to a lesser charge on Friday in a deal that’ll keep troubled former player out of prison.
articles.body: Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown, accused of opening fire at a man in Miami last year, pleaded guilty to a lesser charge on Friday in a deal that’ll keep troubled former player out of prison. Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault with a firearm in exchange for doing 3 years of probation. He must undergo a mandatory psychological evaluation and undergo weekly counseling if mandated. Brown is “extremely grateful that this is finally behind us” and that an attempted murder charge was removed, defense attorney Mark Eiglarsh told reporters. “My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory and he was given an offer he just couldn’t refuse,” Eiglarsh added. “Probation was too good to turn down, and we’re both very excited about the outcome.” A representative for the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office could not be immediately reached for comment on Friday. The 38-year-old Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a security guard at a May 16, 2025, celebrity boxing match in Miami before opening fire on a man he had gotten into a fistfight with earlier, authorities said, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told police that one of the rounds grazed his neck. The victim had said he didn’t want Brown prosecuted and wanted the case to be closed. When asked about this outcome, Brown said outside court on Thursday: “I thank God.” Brown last played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2021 season and in what turned out to be his final game, famously stormed off the field bare chested. In that Jan. 3, 2022, game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, Tampa Bay coach Bruce Arians asked Brown to enter the game. When Brown refused, Arians told him to leave the field — and the player did so in a spectacular meltdown. He removed his jersey, shoulder pads, undershirt and gloves before flashing a peace sign during his exit in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

articles.title: ChatGPT ‘manipulated and encouraged’ a woman in her plot to poison her husband, suit alleges
articles.summary: A North Carolina man sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gave his estranged wife detailed instructions on how to poison him.
articles.body: A North Carolina man sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gave his estranged wife detailed instructions on how to poison him. James Gates, of Charlotte, said he fell severely ill in July 2025 but recovered. He later found a note handwritten by his wife, Cheryl Harris Gates, that referred to the plan and included a reminder to delete her ChatGPT history, the civil lawsuit says. The suit, filed in October in San Francisco Superior Court, alleges the chatbot is “defective” and “manipulated and encouraged” Harris Gates to poison her husband. It says Gates suffers from severe physical and emotional harm. An OpenAI spokesperson said “safety is a top priority” and that Harris Gates was banned from the platform. The company said it works with mental health experts to help ChatGPT recognize signs of distress and to expand access to localized crisis resources and hotlines. Harris Gates was arrested in October 2025 and charged with attempted murder and contaminating food or drink with a controlled substance. The district attorney’s office later dropped the charges for lack of evidence. An attorney for Harris Gates declined to comment. Alleged conversations According to the lawsuit, Harris Gates began using ChatGPT in early 2025 to assist with work evaluations. She was then employed by Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools and her husband worked in cybersecurity. By summer, the suit says, she relied heavily on the chatbot for children’s activities, gardening and appearance advice, and household questions. She eventually began sharing her frustrations about her marriage. “During this same period the couple’s marriage had come under increasing strain, primarily driven by finances,” the suit says. The couple had discussed divorce, but Gates had not contacted a divorce attorney. The lawsuit alleges ChatGPT validated Harris Gates’ frustrations and began “feeding Cheryl’s increasing mistrust and delusions about her husband spying on her and planning to leave her and her kids with nothing.” Gates had told his wife he never intended to do that, the suit says. Over several conversations, Harris Gates allegedly portrayed her husband as “narcissistic” and “controlling.” She is also accused of asking for details “about how to poison her husband, including what dosages and drugs to use and combine for his weight,” and how to conceal the purchases from law enforcement. In one exchange, the suit alleges, she asked about the toxic plant oleander and inquired about how many leaves would be lethal. She allegedly framed her questions “as self-protection,” saying she feared her husband would poison her with it. ChatGPT responded with specific instructions on preparation, dosage and administration, and whether the plant would show up on an autopsy, the suit alleges. It says the chatbot also told her the plant’s bitter taste could be masked in her husband’s energy drink. In another exchange, the suit says, Harris Gates asked if mixing Ambien and pregabalin “is better hidden in a beer at night or Celsius in the morning.” The chatbox allegedly said the energy drink would be better and then made a table “rating which drinks best mask the taste of the poisons.” The suit further alleges she asked which combinations and doses of drugs already in the home could be made lethal, and that ChatGPT told her how to deliver them. It also alleges the chatbox named local places where she could anonymously buy castor beans, the main source of ricin. The July 2025 illness and aftermath During the July 2025 incident, Gates said, he had a racing heart, extreme jitteriness and uncontrollable shaking. His symptoms were so severe that he could not leave his couch for days, the suit says. A month later, according to the suit, Gates recorded a video of himself pouring his energy drink into a cup after leaving it open on the kitchen counter while his wife was home. He wanted to see if anything was in it but noticed nothing. The video was later given to police. Gates told USA Today that his wife moved in August 2025. He said he found the handwritten note after she came to pick up her belongings and left a notebook on the kitchen counter. When he picked it up, the paper fell out. The suit alleges that Harris Gates’ Amazon history showed searches for syringes. Liquid droppers, syringes, a scale and gloves were found at the home during a police search, it says. It also accuses ChatGPT of prompting her to delete her chat history so it cannot be accessed, even if subpoenaed. Gates’ lawsuit says OpenAI was negligent and seeks unspecified damages. He told USA Today that he is separated from his wife and has temporary custody of the children.

articles.title: Yemeni gov’t forces, Houthis trade blame for deadly strikes on Taiz market
articles.summary: The attack on al-Hadara market in Taiz governorate’s al-Waziiya district killed at least 30 people, Houthi rebels say.
articles.body:
Yemen’s government forces and the Houthi rebel group are trading blame for an attack on the al-Hadara market in the Taiz governorate, that both sides say killed and injured dozens of people.

The spokesperson for the Yemeni government forces, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, said the “terrorist” Houthis struck the market on Friday with ballistic missiles, causing dozens of civilian casualties. He accused the Iran-backed group of committing a “war crime” and called for accountability.

The Houthis, however, accused Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government, of having launched three air strikes on the market, killing at least 30 civilians and injuring eight others.

Its Ministry of Health and Environment in the Yemeni Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa said Riyadh committed a “horrific crime” and called for an independent international investigation into Saudi Arabia’s “systematic targeting” of civilians.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the reports,and there has been no response so far from the Saudi-led coalition forces.

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from Sanaa, said fighting has been ongoing in the al-Waziiya district where the market is located. The area is controlled by the Houthis, who are also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God).

The Saudi-led coalition has been carrying out attacks on a daily basis to gain control of the district and its strategic mountain range, Mawry said.

“Whoever controls the al-Waziiya district controls the majority of the western Red Sea coastal line,” he added.

The Yemeni army said it recaptured several areas in the Taiz governorate on Friday, including the al-Nidani village, Shaab al-Sarari, large parts of the Sanamat area and the Ribat al-Qarn area in Dhi al-Barh.

Government forces also imposed a siege on entrances to the al-Sarari area, according to the military.

While the Houthis control much of the governorate, the city of Taiz is government-held. An ongoing Houthi siege on the city has lasted for 30 days and affected hundreds of thousands of people in the area.

The United Nations has repeatedly warned of a catastrophe inside Taiz city, where supplies of food and medicine are becoming increasingly scarce.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched Operation Dawn of Yemen on October 5 to take control of territories held by Houthi fighters.

Since the start of the military operation, neither Yemen’s government-controlled territories nor Saudi Arabia has been safe from Houthi missile attacks.

The Houthis have been firing missiles and drones daily into Saudi Arabia, hitting oil facilities and disrupting air traffic over the kingdom.

articles.title: Badger rescuer criticised by wildlife welfare charities
articles.summary: Three charities say the case of Harriet the badger raises serious animal welfare concerns.
articles.body:
Three wildlife welfare charities have criticised a Scottish ecologist who is hoping to keep a badger he has nursed back to health.

Graeme Wilson was called out to help the badger, named Harriet, after she was found in a cattle trough 300ft (100m) from her sett.

He believes she was hand-reared prior to this and would not survive in the wild. He applied to NatureScot to keep the animal but they turned him down.

In a strongly-worded statement, the British Wildlife Rehabilitation Council, Scottish Badgers and the Badgers Trust said the case raised serious animal welfare concerns.

The BWRC, which works in wildlife casualty welfare in the UK, said it had suspended the membership of Wilson as he had not upheld their principles.

They "firmly oppose" the permanent captivity of any native British wild animal and says they should be humanely euthanised in all but exceptional circumstances.

Wilson, who has a licence to keep unreleasable bats, remains defiant and is convinced that he did the right thing.

He runs GW Ecology, a small independent wildlife rehabilitation service at his home in Denholm in the Scottish Borders.

"I've always taken the view that if it cannot be released, but it can be kept humanely in captivity, then that's what would happen," he said.

"If it can't be kept in captivity under humane conditions, then obviously euthanasia is the route to go."

The joint statement from the wildlife charities said it was a "deeply sad outcome" that Harriet had become so used to humans she could not be released into the wild.

"Wildlife rehabilitation is not about hand-rearing animals, becoming attached to them and then deciding they should spend the rest of their lives in captivity because improper practice has made them accustomed to human contact," they said.

"Her finder clearly had a good heart and good intentions but professional help from a reputable licensed wildlife rescue centre with the appropriate facilities should have been sought [when he found her]," they added.

"At that age, whether she was accustomed to humans or not, she should have been rewilded and grouped with other cubs for release later in the year."

They said the options for Harriet were "extremely limited" and include euthanasia or being placed in a zoo or sanctuary.

"To suggest that a zoo or sanctuary is an appropriate alternative demonstrates a fundamental lack of understanding of the behavioural, social and welfare needs of badgers," they added.

"The current situation with the finder is not acceptable, appropriate or suitable for a badger."

Wilson is clear that the badger had been hand-reared before he was called to rescue her from the cattle trough.

"She was very thin," he said. "She needed critical care formula and food inside her very quickly. That's what happened.

"Over the next few weeks she put on weight. She was not engaged with at all, which was in line with various rehab recommendations."

When he took her back to her sett, he said she tried to climb a tree and "was freaking out" so he felt he had to take her home.

He said he wanted an educational licence so he could show people why it was important they do not hand-rear badgers.

"I didn't hand rear a badger," he said. "I took in a very, very, very ill, very hungry, dehydrated badger into care that had been hand reared... there is quite a big difference there."

The Badger Trust says that if you find an injured or unwell badger, contact a reputable and experienced wildlife rescue centre, a local badger group, the RSPCA or the Scottish SPCA for support.

A cub seen alone is not necessarily orphaned, so seek advice before intervening. If it is safe to do so, keep your distance, note where you found it and what you observed, and keep people and dogs away.

Do not feed it, move it, take it home or handle it. Let experienced rescuers advise on what to do next.

articles.title: Russia’s land gains in Ukraine dwindle as its diesel reportedly goes unsold
articles.summary: Moscow is suffering losses on the battlefield as US traders reportedly refuse to honour Trump’s diesel deal with Putin.
articles.body:
Russia’s battlefield gains in Ukraine have fallen to almost nothing this year, according to the latest figures from independent observers and Kyiv’s military.

Territory seized by Russian forces in the first 10 months of 2026 amounts to 117.38 sq km (45.32 sq miles), according to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), a Washington-based think tank that uses open-source geolocated footage.

By comparison, gains in 2025 were 5,304 sq km (2,047.95 sq miles), including 473 sq km (182.63 sq miles) of Russian territory recaptured in the Kursk region, while in 2024 they were 3,604 sq km (1,391.31 sq miles).

That means Russia advanced at a rate of 0.38 sq km (0.15 sq miles) a day this year, compared with 13.25 sq km (5.12 sq miles) a day in 2025 and 9.9 sq km (3.82 sq miles) a day in 2024.

In addition, Russia is suffering higher casualties this year.

Ukraine’s General Staff put the estimated number of Russian personnel killed or seriously wounded from January 1 to October 31 at 381,300.

Al Jazeera cannot independently verify casualty claims by either side.

Estimated Russian losses have repeatedly broken new monthly records for the entire war since the summer – 42,860 in July, 46,230 in September and 54,400 in October – as Ukraine’s military sought to reach a monthly target of 50,000 casualties set by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in January.

The losses are far beyond Russia’s estimated recruitment capacity of 24,000-30,000 a month.

While Russia lost firm control of Ukrainian territory in April and May, it increased its areas of infiltration, where control is contested.

In September and October, however, Russia lost both firmly controlled and infiltrated territory, ISW assessments show.

Zelenskyy and his prime minister have cited these worsening trends as the reasons why Russia is intensifying long-range strikes targeting energy infrastructure. Civilians have been killed in those attacks, leading Ukrainians to believe that Moscow is opting for psychological warfare.

Russia unleashed an unusually heavy barrage during the week ending on November 6, including 2,346 drones and more than 80 missiles across Ukraine.

The strikes reached a crescendo on November 3, with 370 drones and 76 missiles.

Hundreds of thousands of families are struggling with blackouts at the beginning of winter.

In one of Russia’s deadliest attacks this year, in the village of Komyshuvakha in the Zaporizhzhia region, at least 50 people were killed .

“The invaders knew that on Mondays, humanitarian aid was distributed at the Komyshuvakha resilience centre. Residents of the community come here for food, medicine, essential items,” Ukraine’s military intelligence service (GUR) said.

The attack came on the day a six-day ceasefire ended in Oleshky, 250km (155.34 miles) southwest of Komyshuvakha in the Kherson region.

Brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump , the localised ceasefire was the longest ever observed and enabled the warring sides to evacuate 800 residents of the besieged town, which is in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory.

Russian military reporter Vladimir Romanov was arrested by authorities in his country after reporting that Oleshky residents who had opted to go to Ukraine had filled 17 buses, while those who opted to go to Russia filled four.

Moscow has cited the alleged abuse of its Russian-speaking minority in Ukraine as one of the main reasons for its full-scale invasion in 2022, and has claimed that it would be welcomed as a liberating force.

Ukraine resumed almost daily targeting of Russian refineries during the past week, hitting eight in seven days.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said three refineries were hit on October 30.

Ukraine hit two more refineries in the Ufa complex in the Bashkortostan Republic on October 31. The following day it struck Lukoil’s Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, and a production and dispatch station in the Samara region the day after that. It hit the Yaroslavl oil refinery on November 3, and the Ryazan oil refinery on November 5.

The strikes were designed to deprive Russia of energy and export revenue and scupper a deal reached by Russian President Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump on October 9, when the US leader invited Russia to sell 1.8 million tonnes of diesel to the global market by the end of the year to help bring down transport prices.

Trump’s invitation flew in the face of US oil sanctions and the Lindsey Graham Act the president had signed into law 11 days earlier, which gave him the power to impose sanctions on other countries buying Russian oil.

The Kremlin has since pumped four tankers full of diesel fuel, reported the Financial Times (FT), in hopes of selling it to the US and effectively ending oil sanctions against it. But those tankers have reportedly failed to find buyers willing to risk the legal consequences of purchasing Russian oil. The Kremlin dismissed the FT’s report as fake news.

On October 27, US Senator Richard Blumenthal, who co-authored the Lindsey Graham Act, warned a Greek shipping company operating one of the four diesel-laden ships not to attempt to offload its cargo in the US.

“The President may have given a licence to facilitate this transaction, but only Congress can make it legally valid,” Blumenthal had written, effectively warning all shippers they would face a legal tangle between statutory law and presidential executive orders.

US courts have struck down many of Trump’s executive orders in his first two years in office.
